svg.title: MotorPhen
svg.desc: Four scenes. 1: a walking figure; each of six joints (neck, pelvis, hips, knees) is withheld in turn from a 7-frame window and predicted from the others, and the knee, whose error exceeds the healthy noise floor, is flagged. 2: a paretic knee flexion curve is reconstructed towards the normative range; in 50 stroke survivors reconstruction moved paretic hip and knee towards the normative mean in 8 of 8 comparisons. 3: in 17 held-out healthy adults all four reported angles stayed within 1.5 degrees, yet 21 and 15 of 48 trials were flagged in the two runs. 4: the paretic side was identified with AUROC 0.54 and 0.62 by the model and 0.84 by the side with lower peak knee flexion in swing; no other setting averaged above 0.66.

g.text: A normative gait model that names the joint,
tested where the impaired side is known.

svg.text: 110 able-bodied adults for training · 17 held out · 50 stroke survivors

g.text: Which joint does the model not expect?
Each joint is hidden in turn and predicted from the others.
A joint is flagged when its error exceeds the healthy noise floor.
Flagged joints are rebuilt from the rest
50 stroke survivors: reconstruction moved paretic hip and knee
towards the normative mean in 8 of 8 comparisons (P < 0.05 in 6).
Angles kept, yet many trials flagged
17 held-out adults: reconstruction kept the reported angles, but
a third or more of trials still had a flagged joint.
A one-line clinical rule does better
No setting averaged above 0.66: training size, age range of the
reference, window length (7, 15, 31 frames), ankles, peak statistic.
